svg.title: Choose a runner according to the work a job does — Generate a self-hosted project with separate runners for checks and Docker
svg.text: Choose a runner according to the work a job does
Scenario: Generate a self-hosted project with separate runners for checks and Docker
Run the checks on real runners
Keep the project settings through an update

g.text: Given I generate a self-hosted project using the
saas-linux-medium-amd64 Docker runner tag
Copier keeps the existing runner tag exactly as entered. The project does not need a private
copy of the toolbox to choose its Docker runners.
Then GitLab validates the complete generated pipeline
GitLab resolves the whole generated pipeline. File checks have no tag and no service;
project tasks retain Docker because their commands may start containers.
When I add the web application without changing the generated pipeline
The project Taskfile defines the application tasks. The generated pipeline stays unchanged
and keeps Docker available to those tasks.
Then my project has its own lint settings and two mistakes to catch
The input is visible before the verdict: a project word, a misspelled word, and an insecure
URL. Both project lint hooks must still run.
Then Commitlint passes on the unprivileged runner
The job runs with privileged mode disabled, without a Docker socket or a Docker service. The
real job page identifies its runner; only the bootstrap before the check is collapsed.
And MegaLinter starts directly in its own image on the unprivileged
runner
The job page and the observed container agree: MegaLinter runs directly in its own image
with privileged mode disabled and no Docker socket. Only image preparation is expanded;
GitLab keeps the other log sections folded.
And MegaLinter rejects a spelling mistake and publishes its reports
This is the full spelling report downloaded from the job artifacts. The project dictionary
accepts its own word, but the deliberate spelling mistake still fails the job.
And the security scan also rejects the insecure URL
The full security report points at the HTTP URL in the project source. The security scanner
is active on the ordinary runner too.
When I update the project through Copier and keep my own settings
Copier advances the toolbox version. The Docker runner tag, project dictionary, lint hooks
and Task settings are preserved exactly.
When I correct both mistakes without changing the lint configuration
I fix the misspelled word and switch the URL to HTTPS. The rules, project dictionary and
lint hooks stay in place.
Then MegaLinter passes on the unprivileged runner
The same GitLab job page now shows a passing job. Its image, runner, project hooks and
downloadable reports are unchanged.
And the spelling scan accepts the corrected file
This is the same spelling report as before, downloaded after the correction. The project
dictionary remains active and the scan passes.
And the security scan accepts the corrected HTTPS URL
The same security scanner now passes. The change fixed the source file; no security rule was
disabled.
And the Docker runner builds and tests the web application
The build, deploy and test jobs use the tagged Docker runner. The HTTP test talks to the
running Compose service and checks the response body.
